title: Florida House, District 37
what_it_does: Represents District 37 in the Florida House of Representatives; votes on state laws and the state budget.
decided_note: Open seat: Republican Rep. Susan Plasencia announced she would not seek re-election. Republican Robert Prater and Democrat Jane Aman qualified for the Nov. 3 ballot.
verified_ballot_note: Oviedo Community News (June 17, 2026): 'Republican Robert Prater and Democrat Jane Aman have qualified for the November ballot in the House District 37 race' (https://oviedocommunitynews.org/2026/06/17/whos-on-the-seminole-county-primary-ballot-for-2026/). Seminole County's notice of general election (https://files.floridados.gov/media/710299/2026_nge_sem_english.pdf) could not be read. Research limitation: every WebFetch (Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, Division of Elections, county SOEs, news sites) was blocked and the search budget was capped, so this roster comes only from search-result snippets and should be re-verified against the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

candidates.name: Robert Prater
candidates.occupation: Teacher and dean of students, Orange County Public Schools (20+ years)
candidates.background: Republican candidate for the open HD 37 seat in Seminole County; qualified for the November ballot.

taxes.summary: Lists tax relief and toll relief among affordability priorities.
taxes.quote: Tax relief that puts money back in family budgets

sources.title: Issues — Robert Prater for State Representative, District 37

property_tax.summary: Asked whether he would vote yes or no on Amendment 3, Prater did not state a position, saying the question is for taxpayers to decide. He said he appreciates that the proposal keeps school property taxes intact and bars underfunding police and fire, and that lost revenue should be addressed by scrutinizing local budgets for waste.
property_tax.quote: Every Floridian will soon have the opportunity to weigh in on how our hard-earned money is spent in this state.

sources.title: Robert Prater — Oviedo Community News 2026 general election candidate profile

insurance.summary: Calls for property insurance reform that cracks down on carrier abuse.
insurance.quote: Property insurance reform — cracking down on carrier abuse

sources.title: Issues — Robert Prater for State Representative, District 37

housing.summary: On housing affordability Prater pointed to the One Stop Housing model of converting underused hotels and malls into workforce rentals, public-private partnerships, continued first-time-homebuyer and down-payment assistance, and streamlining permitting across agencies, which he said acts as a tax on housing.
housing.quote: Too often, housing projects face lengthy permitting processes, regulatory hurdles, and coordination challenges between multiple agencies. At the end of the day, that is a tax.

sources.title: Robert Prater — Oviedo Community News 2026 general election candidate profile

immigration.summary: Prater said the federal and state governments must enforce immigration laws and that circumventing the legal immigration process is a practice he does not support, while adding that enforcement agencies must operate within their legal limits and be held accountable if they abuse those powers, and that Congress needs to reform the system.
immigration.quote: We are a nation of laws, and that includes immigration law. ... Circumventing that process is a practice I do not support.

sources.title: Robert Prater — Oviedo Community News 2026 general election candidate profile

abortion.summary: Asked whether Florida's abortion restrictions should be more strict, less strict or stay the same, Prater answered that they should stay the same.

property_tax.summary: In the Oviedo Community News general-election questionnaire (Sept. 30, 2026) Aman said she will vote No on Amendment 3, saying property taxes should be approached 'with a scalpel, not a baseball bat' and that the amendment as written would harm public safety and other critical services.
property_tax.quote: I will vote no. I understand that people absolutely need relief, but I believe we should approach property taxes with a scalpel, not a baseball bat.

environment.summary: Asked to name the biggest environmental issue for state government, Aman said protecting Seminole County's Rural Boundary, which she said maintains sensitive agricultural and conservation land and limits flood risk from overdevelopment. She also said she would vote to protect locally adopted rural boundaries.
environment.quote: The Rural Boundary maintains the integrity of sensitive agricultural and conservation lands. Overdevelopment would have lasting environmental impacts and increase flood risk for existing and future residents.
